question: Can information-theoretic local-environment coverage select fixed-size subsets of atomistic structures that retain more entropy, diversity, outliers, and machine-learning-potential accuracy than random sampling, k-means, or mean-descriptor farthest-point sampling?

key_findings.claim: The proposed selector scores candidate structures by their own entropy plus the single most surprising environment relative to the current subset, then greedily selects a fixed number of structures.
key_findings.evidence: Atomic environments use a fixed two- and three-body distance descriptor with 32 neighbors, 5 A cutoff, Gaussian bandwidth h=0.015 A^-1, KDE entropy H, differential entropy delta H, and diversity D. The procedure starts from the maximum-entropy structure and, until the requested subset size K is reached, selects the structure maximizing max delta H over its environments plus H of that structure.

anchors.section: 2.1 Information entropy and QUESTS method / Equations 1-6
2.4 Minimum set cover / Equation 9 and Algorithm 4

key_findings.claim: On the GAP datasets at 10% size, the method usually has the strongest information metrics and lowest force error, but fullerene overlap exposes a severe coverage failure hidden by entropy and diversity.
key_findings.evidence: At 10%, graphene MSC reports entropy 5.55, diversity 6.34, overlap 0.99, and force error 0.24 eV/A; the three baselines have entropy at most 4.24, diversity at most 5.82, overlap at most 0.98, and force error at least 0.45. Nanotube MSC reports 7.86, 8.09, 0.80, and 0.71 versus baseline maxima 7.00, 7.40, 0.78 and minimum error 0.86. For fullerenes, however, MSC entropy and diversity are both 9.18 and its force error 2.73, while overlap is only 0.08 versus 0.67 random, 0.62 k-means, and 0.41 FPS.

key_findings.claim: The MLIP results do not show one selector systematically winning at every size; even MSC loses on some fixed-budget force tests.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly state that no subsampling algorithm systematically yields the lowest force error, while emphasizing MSC's narrower low-data error range. In the fullerene table at 25%, MSC force error is 3.13 eV/A, worse than random 2.99, k-means 2.96, and mean FPS 3.08. Several TM23 high-fraction entries are also tied or worse, including Ir melt at 75% (MSC 0.80 eV/A versus 0.63 random, 0.68 k-means, 0.76 FPS, and 0.71 full) and Ti melt at 50% (MSC 1.00 versus FPS 0.92 and full 0.88).

key_findings.claim: The strongest MLIP evidence is the low-data TM23 regime, where MSC substantially reduces force error across cold, warm, and melt splits for all four reported elements.
key_findings.evidence: At 10%, MSC errors for Ag cold/warm/melt are 0.02/0.05/0.17 eV/A versus random 0.08/0.23/0.58; for Co they are 0.18/0.30/0.61 versus random 0.32/0.64/1.22; for Ir 0.20/0.34/0.64 versus 0.41/0.82/1.54; and for Ti 0.26/0.37/0.93 versus 0.36/0.55/1.22. K-means and FPS are also worse in those entries.

key_findings.claim: A complete audit of all 64 ColabFit supplementary tables supports the entropy/diversity claim much more strongly than the overlap claim, especially at high compression.
key_findings.evidence: Against the best of random, k-means, and mean FPS in each rounded table, MSC's entropy win/tie/loss counts at 10%, 25%, 50%, and 75% are 54/2/8, 53/2/9, 55/0/9, and 50/0/14. Diversity counts are 59/1/4, 61/2/1, 50/7/7, and 32/22/10. Overlap counts are only 22/9/33, 34/15/15, 28/29/7, and 18/45/1. Thus at 10% MSC loses overlap on 33 of 64 datasets despite the abstract's unqualified claim that it consistently preserves coverage-like outliers.

key_findings.claim: Several low-data overlap failures are not marginal: the chosen subset can cover far fewer original environments than a random subset of the same size.
key_findings.evidence: At 10% in the FitSNAP Fe NPJ2021 table, MSC overlap is 0.11 versus 0.77 random; for Fe nanoparticles it is 0.27 versus 0.64; and for mlearn Li it is 0.21 versus 0.51. These failures coexist with generally higher entropy or diversity, showing that the three proposed efficiency measures are not interchangeable and that maximizing the selection score does not guarantee overlap.

anchors.section: Supporting Information / Fe nanoparticle and FitSNAP Fe tables

key_findings.claim: Calling the fixed-budget heuristic a minimum-set-cover solver is not supported by its stated objective or by a set-cover guarantee.
key_findings.evidence: Classical minimum set cover defines a discrete universe and subsets, stops when the universe is covered, and greedily chooses the subset covering the most uncovered elements. Algorithm 4 instead accepts a prescribed K, ranks each candidate using only its most surprising environment plus within-structure entropy, and stops after K structures. It specifies neither a discrete coverage relation nor an uncovered-element count, approximation factor, proof, or termination at full cover. It is therefore a novel coverage-inspired fixed-cardinality heuristic, not a demonstrated solution of minimum set cover.

anchors.section: 2.4 Minimum set cover / Equation 9 and Algorithm 4
2.4 Minimum set cover analogy and fixed-target description

key_findings.claim: The differential-entropy containment test is cardinality-sensitive, so raw overlap across reference-set sizes can conflate support with sample count and duplication.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 6 uses minus log of the unnormalized sum of kernels over every reference environment, whereas Equation 4 divides its KDE sum by N. Adding duplicate or nearby reference environments can therefore drive delta H downward and convert a point from 'surprising' to 'contained' even when geometric support is unchanged. Fixed-size comparisons between selectors are less affected, but overlap across compression fractions or structures with different atom counts is not a cardinality-invariant support measure.

anchors.section: 2.1 Information entropy and QUESTS method / Equations 4-6

key_findings.claim: The paper's force-CDF interpretation has its direction reversed under the CDF definition it gives.
key_findings.evidence: The text defines the cumulative distribution as the fraction of forces x below a threshold f. At a fixed high threshold, a distribution with a longer high-force tail has more mass above f and therefore a lower, not higher, CDF value. The paper and figure discussion instead describe a higher force CDF as preserving a longer tail, so this diagnostic's verbal interpretation is internally inconsistent even if the plotted curves remain directly inspectable.

3.1 GAP-20 case study / Figure 2 force CDF discussion

key_findings.claim: The reported method rankings have no demonstrated robustness to stochastic baseline initialization or MLIP training variation.
key_findings.evidence: Random sampling is stochastic, k-means chooses a random member per cluster, and mean FPS is randomly initialized, yet the tables report one value per selector without repeated subset draws or error bars. SevenNet results likewise report no independent training seeds. The authors acknowledge that model training and test distributions are variable, so small ranking differences cannot be distinguished from selection or training noise.

key_findings.claim: The equal-structure-epoch training design leaves an optimization-schedule confound that can disproportionately affect the headline 10% regime.
key_findings.evidence: The 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% models receive 10000, 4000, 2000, 1333, and 1000 epochs, respectively, to equalize nominal structure presentations. But the 10% models use batch size 4 while the others use 40, and the learning rate is multiplied by 0.99 per epoch. Consequently subset fractions see very different optimizer-step counts and decay trajectories; equal structure-epochs do not make optimization exposure equivalent.

key_findings.claim: The train/test protocol is not described consistently enough to rule out split-selection ambiguity.
key_findings.evidence: The methods say each subsampled dataset is randomly split 80:10:10 and that a single test set is shared by all models, while the supporting text says models trained on compressed GAP subsets are tested on the original full datasets and TM captions refer to original test splits. It is unclear whether selection occurs before or after fixing the common test set and whether the original 'full dataset' means its held-out test partition or all structures. A test structure eligible for selection would invalidate the claimed held-out comparison.

key_findings.claim: Diversity is explicitly an unproved approximation and need not behave monotonically as points are added, limiting its interpretation as exact phase-space support.
key_findings.evidence: The main text states that D approximates distribution support and has not been mathematically proven exact. The supplement further explains that adding environments can change the differential-entropy terms of existing points, so diversity is not guaranteed to increase monotonically. It remains a useful heuristic diagnostic, but the paper cannot use it as an exact coverage certificate.

key_findings.claim: The validation remains single-element and descriptor-specific, while compute grows with the number of environments.
key_findings.evidence: All 64 ColabFit validation datasets are single-element, as are the highlighted GAP and TM23 cases. The fixed distance descriptor does not encode chemical identity, and no multicomponent, molecular, reactive, or compositional-transfer experiment is reported. The authors also report CPU-hour-scale runs for roughly 10^5 to 10^6 environments, versus minutes for smaller datasets, and note a GPU implementation; scaling to foundation-model corpora is not demonstrated.

method.core_idea: Represent every atomic environment explicitly, quantify novelty with a kernel information measure, and greedily select whole structures that combine high internal entropy with at least one environment not yet represented by the current subset.
method.mechanism: For each atom, concatenate sorted two-body neighbor distances and averaged three-body neighbor terms. Compute KDE entropy H, differential entropy delta H relative to a selected environment pool, diversity D, and overlap under delta H <= 0. Initialize with the highest-entropy structure, repeatedly choose the candidate maximizing its largest environment-level delta H plus its structure entropy, and stop at a user-specified number K. Compare the resulting subset with random sampling, k-means with one random structure per cluster, and randomly initialized farthest-point sampling over mean structure descriptors; then train SevenNet on selected GAP-20 and TM23 subsets.
assumptions: The fixed 32-neighbor, 5 A distance descriptor and bandwidth h=0.015 A^-1 preserve the distinctions relevant to energies, forces, and structural outliers.
One maximally surprising environment plus within-structure entropy is an adequate proxy for the marginal coverage gained by adding an entire structure.
The threshold delta H <= 0 defines meaningful containment despite the unnormalized reference-kernel sum and its dependence on reference cardinality.
High-force environments are usually useful structural outliers rather than label noise, numerical failures, or physically irrelevant collisions.
A fixed structure count is an appropriate budget even when structures vary greatly in atom count, memory footprint, and number of environments.
One run of each stochastic selector and one SevenNet training run adequately represent method performance.
Equal nominal structure-epochs make training effort comparable across subset fractions despite different batch sizes, update counts, and epoch-based learning-rate decay.
Single-element benchmarks are representative of multicomponent and chemically diverse training-set compression.

techniques.role: Encodes every atom using sorted, cutoff-weighted neighbor distances and averaged neighbor-neighbor distances without collapsing a structure to one mean before novelty scoring.
Measures redundancy in an environment set with a fixed-bandwidth Gaussian kernel density estimate.
Labels an environment as represented when its negative log summed kernel similarity to the reference set is nonpositive.
Evaluates compression using three model-free summaries of redundancy, approximate support size, and reference containment.
Selects fixed-budget structures by adding within-structure entropy to the maximum environment novelty relative to the selected set.
Tests whether information-metric gains transfer to equivariant neural interatomic-potential force accuracy.

evaluations.setting: GAP-20 graphene, nanotube, and fullerene subsets at 10%, 25%, 50%, and 75% of the original structure count.
evaluations.metric: Entropy, diversity, original-data overlap, and SevenNet force mean absolute error in eV/A.
evaluations.result: MSC is especially strong at 10% for entropy/diversity and force error, but fullerene 10% overlap is 0.08 versus 0.67 random, and fullerene 25% force error is the worst of the four selectors at 3.13.
evaluations.baseline: Random sampling, k-means plus a random member per cluster, mean-descriptor FPS, and the full dataset.

evaluations.setting: TM23 Ag, Co, Ir, and Ti compressed subsets evaluated on cold, warm, and melt test splits.
evaluations.metric: SevenNet force mean absolute error in eV/A.
evaluations.result: MSC has large gains across all twelve element-temperature combinations at 10%, but at higher fractions several entries tie or lose; Ir melt at 75% is 0.80 versus 0.63 random and 0.71 full.
evaluations.baseline: The same three compressed-data selectors and full-data training.

evaluations.setting: All 64 single-element ColabFit datasets at four retained fractions, audited from Tables S20-S83.
evaluations.metric: Count of MSC wins/ties/losses against the best baseline in each rounded table for entropy, diversity, and overlap.
evaluations.baseline: Best rounded result among random, k-means, and mean FPS at the same fraction.

evaluations.setting: GAP-20 and ColabFit structural-outlier inspection with force cumulative distributions and UMAP projections.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative preservation of rare environments and high-force tails.
evaluations.result: Chosen examples show MSC retaining visually isolated environments and extreme-force structures that mean-structure baselines miss, but the CDF direction is described inconsistently and no aggregate outlier-recall statistic or uncertainty is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Random, k-means, mean FPS, and two-dimensional UMAP visualization.

evaluations.setting: Runtime characterization for QUESTS selection on datasets of different environment counts.
evaluations.metric: Reported wall-clock scale on CPU and qualitative GPU availability.
evaluations.result: Smaller cases run in minutes on a laptop, while about 10^5 to 10^6 environments require CPU hours; a GPU implementation is available, but memory scaling and foundation-scale results are absent.
evaluations.baseline: No matched runtime or memory comparison with DIRECT, CUR/FPS, active learning, or learned-embedding selectors.

limitations: Author-stated: diversity is an approximation rather than a mathematically exact support measure and is not guaranteed to be monotone.
Author-stated: no compression algorithm systematically achieves the smallest MLIP force error, although MSC is more reliable in several low-data cases.
Author-stated: high-force environments are useful outlier proxies for the studied trajectory data, not a universal definition of physically important rarity.
Author-stated: selection can require CPU hours at 10^5 to 10^6 environments, with GPU acceleration offered for larger workloads.
Reviewer-identified: Algorithm 4 is a fixed-K coverage-inspired heuristic and lacks the discrete universe, stopping criterion, proof, or approximation guarantee needed to establish minimum set cover.

Reviewer-identified: low-fraction overlap loses to the best baseline in 33 of 64 ColabFit tables at 10% and 15 of 64 at 25%, contradicting an unqualified claim of consistently retained coverage/outliers.
Reviewer-identified: overlap inherits sample-count and duplication sensitivity from the unnormalized sum in Equation 6.
Reviewer-identified: fixed h, cutoff, neighbor count, and descriptor family receive no sensitivity or ablation study.
Reviewer-identified: random, k-means, and FPS baselines are stochastic but have no repeated selection seeds or error bars; MLIP training uncertainty is also unreported.

Reviewer-identified: equal structure-epochs do not equalize optimizer steps or learning-rate schedules because the 10% subset uses a tenfold smaller batch and every model decays learning rate per epoch.
Reviewer-identified: train/subset/test ordering and the meaning of the 'original full dataset' test are described ambiguously across the methods and table captions.
Reviewer-identified: all validation datasets are single-element, so multicomponent chemistry, element identity, reactions, molecules, and composition-shift coverage remain untested.
Reviewer-identified: the UMAP demonstration compares selected examples qualitatively and does not prove that all conventional learned or reduced representations cannot quantify coverage.
Reviewer-identified: the paper reports no matched selection-runtime comparison, label-generation savings, total training cost, or accuracy-versus-compute Pareto curve.
failure_modes: A structure with one isolated descriptor can dominate the maximum-novelty term even if that environment is corrupted, unphysical, mislabeled, or irrelevant to the desired potential.
A structure containing many moderately novel environments can lose to one containing a single extreme environment because Equation 9 uses a maximum rather than total marginal coverage.
Duplicate reference environments lower delta H through the unnormalized kernel sum and can create artificial containment without expanding geometric support.
Counting structures rather than environments, atoms, bytes, or training FLOPs can select a subset that meets K but exceeds the intended computational budget.
Fixed bandwidth and Euclidean distance can merge distinct chemical environments or fragment equivalent ones when descriptor scales, density, or composition change.
A high-entropy subset can have poor original-data overlap, as the 10% fullerene and several ColabFit cases demonstrate.
Information-metric improvements need not yield lower force error at higher subset fractions or under another model architecture.
A random seed for the baseline or MLIP optimizer could reverse small differences because only point estimates are reported.
If selection sees structures later used for testing, coverage and force results can be optimistic; the documented split order does not fully exclude this scenario.
The descriptor cannot distinguish species in a multicomponent system as currently stated, so chemically different local environments with similar geometry may collide.
Extreme-force retention can preserve numerical pathologies or short-range collisions rather than valuable physical states.
Quadratic-like kernel comparisons over many environments can become a memory or runtime bottleneck before foundation-scale atomistic corpora are reached.
reusable_insights: Evaluate atomistic compression at the environment level even when the selectable unit is a whole structure; mean structure embeddings can hide rare atoms in large cells.
Report redundancy, approximate support, and held-out task error separately because high entropy, high diversity, high overlap, and low force error can disagree sharply.
Audit every supplementary benchmark rather than relying on representative plots; the 64-table count here changes the interpretation of the overlap claim.
Normalize or otherwise calibrate density-based containment when reference-set cardinality changes, and test invariance to duplicated points.
Match subset methods by the true resource budget: number of environments, atoms, bytes, label cost, and optimizer steps can be more meaningful than structure count.
Repeat every stochastic selection baseline and every downstream training run, reporting distributional uncertainty rather than one table entry.
Coverage-inspired selection should define its universe and marginal-coverage objective explicitly if set-cover terminology or guarantees are invoked.
Outlier preservation needs a task-specific validity filter so informative rare states are distinguished from corrupted or unphysical extremes.
open_questions: Does a true submodular coverage objective or explicit set-cover formulation outperform the maximum-delta-H heuristic at equal environment and compute budgets?
How do results change when Equation 6 is normalized by reference count or calibrated to a fixed false-containment rate?
Are the ColabFit entropy/diversity wins and overlap losses stable over repeated random, k-means, FPS, and MSC tie-breaking seeds?
Does the method retain its advantage when the split is fixed before selection and every selector is forbidden from observing test structures?
Which bandwidths, neighbor counts, cutoffs, learned descriptors, and species-aware kernels work for multicomponent reactive datasets?
Does selecting by total marginal environment coverage improve the severe 10% overlap failures without sacrificing rare-force states?
How do downstream conclusions change under MACE, NequIP, GAP, and foundation MLIPs rather than one SevenNet configuration?
What accuracy-versus-wall-clock and accuracy-versus-label-cost frontier does QUESTS achieve against DIRECT, CUR/FPS, active learning, and gradient-guided selection?
Can high-force outliers be screened for physical validity before they receive priority?
Why do information gains cease to predict force-error gains for several 25-75% subsets?

competitive_landscape.title: Automatic Selection of Atomic Fingerprints and Reference Configurations for Machine-Learning Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: Imbalzano et al. use CUR decomposition and farthest-point sampling to select informative atomic fingerprints and reference configurations. The reviewed paper instead scores every local environment with fixed-bandwidth information measures while selecting whole structures, emphasizing rare environments that mean structure representations can suppress; it does not provide a matched runtime, uncertainty, or multicomponent comparison against CUR.

competitive_landscape.title: An Entropy-Maximization Approach to Automated Training Set Generation for Interatomic Potentials
competitive_landscape.difference: Karabin and Perez bias structural search toward maximum entropy to generate diverse interatomic-potential training configurations. The reviewed work compresses an already generated structure pool with local KDE novelty and a fixed structure budget; it cannot discover configurations absent from that pool but is model- and label-free during selection.

competitive_landscape.title: Robust Training of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials with Dimensionality Reduction and Stratified Sampling
competitive_landscape.difference: DIRECT clusters dimension-reduced, pretrained M3GNet structure features and samples strata, with demonstrations on large and chemically diverse data. The reviewed paper avoids collapsing each structure to a learned global feature and supplies environment-level information metrics, but validates only single-element data and does not compare scale, chemistry, runtime, or force accuracy head to head.

competitive_landscape.title: Model-free quantification of completeness, uncertainties, and outliers in atomistic machine learning using information theory
competitive_landscape.difference: This prior work from the same group already introduces the local descriptor, information entropy, differential-entropy completeness, diversity, and model-free uncertainty/outlier analysis. The reviewed paper's incremental contribution is the Equation 9 fixed-budget selection heuristic plus extensive compression and MLIP experiments, not the underlying information measures themselves.

competitive_landscape.title: Unsupervised Atomic Data Mining via Multi-Kernel Graph Autoencoders for Machine Learning Force Fields
competitive_landscape.difference: The graph-autoencoder approach learns multi-kernel structural embeddings and mines clusters to prune force-field data. The reviewed selector is cheaper to define, deterministic conditional on ties, and does not train a representation, but inherits a fixed handcrafted geometry and bandwidth and provides no direct comparison on chemically heterogeneous datasets.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient-Guided Furthest Point Sampling for Robust Training Set Selection
competitive_landscape.difference: Gradient-guided FPS uses force or gradient information to prioritize samples whose labels induce distinct learning signals and reports bootstrap-style robustness analyses. The reviewed paper is label- and model-free and can select before expensive force computation, but its geometry-only novelty can miss label variation and its one-run baselines do not establish statistical robustness.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims an information-theoretic minimum-set-cover algorithm that finds the smallest structure subset spanning the original environment distribution, consistently preserving outliers, diversity, force tails, and low-data MLIP accuracy better than standard subsampling across GAP-20, TM23, and 64 ColabFit datasets.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Equation 9 and Algorithm 4 add a new greedy whole-structure selector to previously published QUESTS information measures. The strongest aggregate evidence is entropy and diversity: at 10%, MSC beats or ties the best baseline on 56 of 64 entropy tables and 60 of 64 diversity tables, and it yields large 10% TM23 force improvements. However, it loses overlap on 33 of 64 tables at 10%, fails fullerene overlap at 0.08, and does not systematically win force error.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The useful novelty is a simple local-environment-aware, fixed-budget compression heuristic and an unusually broad information-metric benchmark. It is not established as minimum set cover: there is no explicit universe, marginal uncovered-set objective, coverage stopping rule, proof, or approximation guarantee. The evidence supports strong redundancy removal and approximate diversity retention, plus promising low-data MLIP behavior, but not the abstract's universal coverage/outlier language, exact support preservation, multicomponent generality, or statistically robust superiority. The underlying entropy, differential entropy, diversity, and descriptor are inherited from the authors' arXiv:2404.12367v2 work.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text audit of all 76 pages of arXiv:2511.10561v1: 17-page main paper, references, all supporting methods, figures, and Tables S1-S83. The cached PDF is byte-identical to the current official versioned arXiv PDF checked on 2026-08-23. The 64-table win/tie/loss counts were independently recomputed from the official v1 HTML tables using their rounded values; ties are recorded rather than forced into wins. Six current competitors were checked against official arXiv revision histories. Equation, algorithm, negative-result, split, stochasticity, optimization, and CDF-direction claims are explicitly attributed as author-reported, reviewer-inference, or contradiction-audit. No independent second reviewer has passage-checked this record, so it remains full_text with primary-full-text-v1 rather than verified.
